title: Catharinus: private divine faith of remitted sins possible without being Catholic faith-act
source_text: XXXIV. Ambrosius Catharinus autem qui Concilio Tridentino ut Episcopus interfuit, negat quidem persuasionem, quam quis habet de obtenta a Deo peccatorum suorum venia & remissione, esse fidei Catholicae actum, aut omnino aliquid ad justificationem hominis requisitum; sed tamen existimat quemlibet justificatum, sine peculiari revelatione, posse fide divina, non Catholica, sed privata, certo credere sibi esse remissa peccata, dum scilicet in se sentit & experitur ea sub quorum conditione Deus nobis in verbo promisit peccatorum remissionem. Ut enim assensus aliquis censeatur esse divinae fidei, non opus esse ut revelationi proxime innitatur, & ab ea solum oriatur, sed sufficere si colligatur ex principiis revelatis, junctis aliis quae experimento, aut alia ratione evidenter nota sunt, prout Catharini sententiam explicat Vasquez, in 1. 2. Difput. 209. cap. 3.
pass_a_gloss: Ambrosius Catharinus, however, who took part in the Council of Trent as a bishop, does deny that the persuasion someone has of having obtained from God the pardon and remission of his sins is an act of Catholic faith, or anything at all required for a person justification; yet he thinks any justified person, without a special revelation, can by divine faith — not Catholic but private — firmly believe that his sins are remitted to him, namely when he feels and experiences in himself those things under whose condition God promised us in the Word the remission of sins. For an assent to be counted as divine faith, it need not rest immediately on revelation and arise from it alone; it suffices if it is gathered from revealed principles joined to other things that are evidently known by experience or another reason, as Vasquez explains Catharinus view (in 1.2 Disp. 209, c. 3).
pass_b_english: Catharinus denies that persuasion of obtained pardon is an act of Catholic faith or a requirement for justification.

Yet he allows the justified, without special revelation, a private divine faith that their sins are remitted when they experience in themselves the conditions under which God promised remission; Vasquez notes such assent can be divine faith if drawn from revealed principles plus evident experience (Disp. 209.3).

lemmas.latin: fide divina, non Catholica, sed privata
lemmas.gloss: by divine faith, not Catholic, but private

choices.why: Catharinus middle path vs Catholic-faith act.
rejected: remitted-sins certainty as Catholic faith-act required for justification
